key_insight: Predicting time increments with an improved Fourier Neural Operator yields a more accurate and compact surrogate for 2D Rayleigh-Bénard convection than a standard full-solution FNO.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, low-memory CFD surrogates for convection-driven flows, supporting rapid simulation, screening, and reduced-cost modeling workflows.
method: Use a Fourier Neural Operator to learn the convection dynamics in spectral space.
Predict the next time increment rather than the entire state to improve accuracy.
Benchmark against a standard FNO baseline on 2D Rayleigh-Bénard convection.
evidence_signal: The model is reported at 314k parameters, 1.26 MB, and 7 ms inference while maintaining similar benchmark accuracy to prior results.
watch_item: Generalization to finer meshes is possible, but accuracy is still constrained by the resolution of the training data.
paper_title: Fourier Neural Operators for Rayleigh-Bénard Convection
